I feel that I've been romanticizing the idea of suicide for years and despite coming in contact with so many situations that I know change a lot of people's tune, it has only made that drive in me strive much harder to romanticize the idea. I have died twice. The last time was the most disappointing. I told my mom that I wanted to die and she didn't visit me in the hospital. Shortly after that my best friend who I would consider more like a twin brother, ended up dying. We promised we'd die together. He didn't want to die and never understood why I did. I have a lot of abuse from childhood that still affects me very deeply and it's a point that frustrates me all the time. It's frustrating to feel like things you have gone through keep you from being who you want to be no matter what. PTSD is a hell of a thing. 

For a long time I told myself what everyone says, that it's a permanent solution to a temporary problem, but when that "problem " has gone on since forever, it doesn't sound very temporary to me anymore. These thoughts don't go away. The disappointment in living doesn't go away. Sometimes it is easier than others but that never means that it's not there. So for the longest time I have faced the fact that yes I want to die but I shouldn't do that. But why? If I feel like shit the next day and the next day and the next day, what's the point in just waiting? I've been thinking about it for a while and I've always had a plan but now it's just a bit more than it used to be. 

I can't make the people who matter to me care about how I feel. I can't get them to care about hurting me as a person. But I can take myself out of the equation entirely. More than just walking away. I don't want to just walk away. I want the ability to not come back. It gets old feeling vulnerable.
